tasks.task_name: Define core team structure and composition
tasks.description:
Establish the core team structure for the project as specified in section 6.1 of the requirement specification. The team should consist of 4-5 people with clearly defined roles:

- 1 Product Manager
- 1 Technical Lead
- 2 Backend/CLI Developers
- 1 Quality Assurance specialist

This task involves documenting the organizational structure, defining reporting relationships, and ensuring all required roles are identified and allocated. The structure should support efficient collaboration and clear ownership of different project areas including product management, technical architecture, implementation, and quality assurance.

This is a foundational organizational task that must be completed before role-specific responsibilities can be assigned and work can begin on the CLI tool development.
tasks.task_notes: This is a prerequisite for all other role-specific tasks. The team structure should be flexible enough to accommodate the range of 4-5 people. Consider whether roles can be combined if only 4 people are available.

requirement_snippets:
Project Team (4-5 people)
├── Product Manager (1)
├── Technical Lead (1)
├── Backend/CLI Developer (2)
└── Quality Assurance (1)
success_criteria: All five role categories defined and assigned

tasks.task_name: Define Product Manager role responsibilities and deliverables
tasks.description:
Define the complete Product Manager role as specified in section 6.2.1 of the requirement specification. The Product Manager is responsible for bridging business requirements with technical implementation.

**Core Responsibilities:**
- Define and prioritize feature roadmap for the CLI tool
- Gather user requirements and feedback from stakeholders
- Coordinate between stakeholders and development team
- Manage project timeline and milestones
- Ensure business requirements are met throughout development
- Create user documentation and marketing materials

**MVP Deliverables:**
The Product Manager must produce the following deliverables for the MVP phase:
- User stories and acceptance criteria for all features
- MVP scope definition with clear boundaries
- User testing plan including test scenarios and success metrics
- Go-to-market strategy for CLI tool launch

This role is critical for ensuring the CLI tool meets user needs and business objectives while maintaining alignment between technical and product perspectives.
tasks.task_notes: The Product Manager role is particularly important for the MVP phase as they define scope and acceptance criteria. Consider whether this person should have prior CLI tool experience or domain expertise in the problem space. The go-to-market strategy should account for the target audience (developers vs. end users) and distribution channels (package managers, GitHub releases, etc.).

tasks.task_name: Define Technical Lead role responsibilities and deliverables
tasks.description:
Define the complete Technical Lead role as specified in section 6.2.2 of the requirement specification. The Technical Lead is responsible for technical excellence and architectural decisions for the CLI tool.

**Core Responsibilities:**
- Architecture design and technical decisions for the CLI tool and Notion integration
- Code review and establishment of quality standards
- Implementation of core modules (hands-on development)
- Integration with Notion API including authentication and data synchronization
- Performance and security oversight across the codebase
- Mentoring other developers on the team

The Technical Lead role combines hands-on development with architectural oversight and team mentorship. This person should have deep expertise in CLI development, API integrations, and software architecture. They are responsible for both writing critical code and ensuring the overall technical quality of the project.

The role requires balancing individual contribution (implementing core modules) with team leadership (code review, mentoring, and technical decision-making).
tasks.task_notes: The MVP deliverables section for Technical Lead appears to be truncated in the provided requirements. The Technical Lead should work closely with the Product Manager to translate business requirements into technical architecture. Consider whether this person should also define technical deliverables such as architecture documentation, API integration specifications, and coding standards. The dual role of individual contributor and technical leader requires careful time management.

- Performance and security oversight

tasks.task_name: Create user stories and acceptance criteria for MVP features
tasks.description:
As specified in the Product Manager MVP deliverables (section 6.2.1), create comprehensive user stories and acceptance criteria for all features planned for the MVP release of the CLI tool.

This deliverable is a key output from the Product Manager role and serves as the foundation for development work. Each user story should follow best practices (e.g., "As a [user type], I want [goal] so that [benefit]") and include specific, testable acceptance criteria.

The user stories should cover all aspects of the CLI tool functionality, including:
- Installation and setup
- Configuration and authentication with Notion
- Core CLI commands and operations
- Error handling and user feedback
- Help and documentation access

Acceptance criteria must be specific, measurable, and testable to enable the QA team to validate implementation.
tasks.task_notes: This is a critical input to all implementation tasks. The quality and completeness of user stories directly impacts development efficiency and product quality. Consider using a standardized format (e.g., Gherkin syntax for acceptance criteria) to improve clarity and testability. These stories should be reviewed and approved by stakeholders before implementation begins.

requirement_snippets:
**MVP Deliverables:**
- User stories and acceptance criteria
- MVP scope definition
- User testing plan
- Go-to-market strategy for CLI tool

All MVP features covered by user stories

tasks.task_name: Define MVP scope and feature boundaries
tasks.description:
As specified in the Product Manager MVP deliverables (section 6.2.1), create a clear MVP scope definition that establishes boundaries for the initial release of the CLI tool.

This deliverable must clearly articulate:
- Which features are IN SCOPE for MVP
- Which features are OUT OF SCOPE (deferred to future releases)
- Feature priorities within the MVP
- Technical and functional boundaries
- Success metrics for MVP launch

The MVP scope definition serves as a contract between the product team and development team, preventing scope creep and ensuring the team focuses on delivering core value quickly. It should balance user needs with technical feasibility and project timeline constraints.

The scope definition should reference the user stories created in the previous task and identify which stories constitute the minimum viable product.
tasks.task_notes: MVP scope definition requires balancing multiple competing concerns: user value, technical complexity, timeline, and resource constraints. The scope should be ambitious enough to provide real value but constrained enough to be achievable with 4-5 people. Consider creating a feature matrix that maps features to effort and value to support prioritization decisions.

- User testing plan
- Go-to-market strategy for CLI tool
success_criteria: In-scope and out-of-scope features clearly identified

tasks.task_name: Develop user testing plan for CLI tool
tasks.description:
As specified in the Product Manager MVP deliverables (section 6.2.1), create a comprehensive user testing plan for the CLI tool.

The testing plan should cover:
- User testing methodology (e.g., usability testing, beta testing, dogfooding)
- Target user segments and recruitment strategy
- Test scenarios and tasks for users to complete
- Success metrics and evaluation criteria
- Feedback collection mechanisms
- Timeline for user testing activities
- Process for incorporating feedback into the product

The user testing plan should focus on validating that the CLI tool meets user needs and is usable by the target audience. It should complement technical QA testing by focusing on user experience, workflow integration, and real-world usage patterns.

The plan should be executable within the MVP timeline and resource constraints.
tasks.task_notes: User testing is critical for CLI tools since command-line interfaces can have steep learning curves. Consider testing with both experienced CLI users and those newer to command-line tools. The testing plan should account for different operating systems (Linux, macOS, Windows) and different shell environments. Plan for multiple rounds of testing: early prototype testing, feature-complete testing, and pre-launch validation.

- User testing plan
- Go-to-market strategy for CLI tool

tasks.task_name: Create go-to-market strategy for CLI tool
tasks.description:
As specified in the Product Manager MVP deliverables (section 6.2.1), develop a comprehensive go-to-market strategy for the CLI tool launch.

The strategy should address:
- Target audience identification and segmentation
- Value proposition and key messaging
- Distribution channels (package managers: npm, pip, homebrew, etc.)
- Launch timeline and phases
- Marketing and promotional activities
- Documentation and support resources
- Adoption metrics and success indicators
- Community building and feedback channels

For a CLI tool specifically, the go-to-market strategy should consider:
- Developer-focused marketing channels (GitHub, Dev.to, Hacker News, etc.)
- Integration with existing developer workflows
- Comparison with existing tools or solutions
- Installation simplicity and onboarding experience

The strategy should be realistic given team size and resources, while maximizing initial adoption and user engagement.
tasks.task_notes: The go-to-market strategy should be developed in parallel with the MVP scope definition to ensure launch readiness. For CLI tools, word-of-mouth and developer community engagement are often more effective than traditional marketing. Consider a phased launch: private beta → public beta → general availability. The strategy should include plans for gathering and responding to early user feedback.

tasks.task_name: Design CLI architecture and technical decisions
tasks.description:
As specified in the Technical Lead responsibilities (section 6.2.2), design the architecture and make foundational technical decisions for the CLI tool.

This task encompasses:
- Overall CLI architecture design (command structure, plugin system, configuration management)
- Technology stack selection (programming language, frameworks, libraries)
- Design patterns and coding standards
- Module structure and separation of concerns
- Error handling and logging strategies
- Testing strategy and framework selection
- Build and deployment pipeline design
- Version management and release process

The architecture should support:
- Integration with Notion API
- Extensibility for future features
- Cross-platform compatibility
- Performance requirements
- Security best practices
- Maintainability and code quality

The Technical Lead should document all major technical decisions with rationale, trade-offs, and alternatives considered. This documentation serves as a reference for the development team and ensures consistency in implementation.
tasks.task_notes: Architecture decisions made here will impact all subsequent development work. The Technical Lead should consider industry best practices for CLI tools (e.g., POSIX compliance, 12-factor app principles) and Notion API specific requirements (rate limiting, authentication, webhook handling). Document architectural decision records (ADRs) for major choices. The architecture should be reviewed with the team before implementation begins.

- Implementation of core modules
- Integration with Notion API
- Performance and security oversight
- Mentoring other developers

tasks.task_name: Establish code review process and quality standards
tasks.description:
As specified in the Technical Lead responsibilities (section 6.2.2), establish a comprehensive code review process and quality standards for the project.

This task includes defining:
- Code review workflow and tools (e.g., GitHub PR process, review checklists)
- Code quality standards (style guides, linting rules, formatting)
- Documentation requirements (inline comments, API docs, README)
- Testing requirements (unit test coverage, integration tests, e2e tests)
- Security review practices
- Performance benchmarks and acceptance criteria
- Definition of done for pull requests

The process should be appropriate for a small team (4-5 people) while maintaining high quality standards. It should facilitate knowledge sharing and mentoring while not creating excessive overhead that slows development.

The Technical Lead should also set up automated tooling where possible (linters, formatters, CI/CD pipelines) to enforce standards consistently.
tasks.task_notes: Quality standards should be established early to prevent technical debt accumulation. For a small team, keep the process lightweight but effective. Consider pair programming for complex modules as an alternative to async code review. The Technical Lead should lead by example in code reviews and use them as mentoring opportunities. Balance perfectionism with pragmatism to maintain development velocity.

tasks.description:
As specified in the Technical Lead responsibilities (section 6.2.2), implement the core modules of the CLI tool. This is a hands-on development task led by the Technical Lead.

Core modules typically include:
- Command parser and argument handling
- Configuration management system
- Authentication and credential management
- Core business logic for primary commands
- Logging and error handling infrastructure
- Plugin or extension system (if in scope)
- Output formatting and display

The Technical Lead should implement the most critical and complex modules personally, serving as reference implementations for the Backend/CLI Developers. The code should exemplify the quality standards and architectural patterns defined for the project.

This implementation work should be done in parallel with the Backend/CLI Developers working on other modules, with the Technical Lead providing guidance and code review.
tasks.task_notes: The Technical Lead should prioritize implementing foundational modules that other developers will depend on. Consider implementing a reference command end-to-end to validate the architecture before the team builds out all features. The implementation should include comprehensive tests and documentation to serve as examples for the team. Balance hands-on coding with code review and mentoring responsibilities.

tasks.description:
As specified in the Technical Lead responsibilities (section 6.2.2), implement the integration with the Notion API. This is a critical component that enables the CLI tool to interact with Notion workspaces.

The integration should include:
- Notion API client setup and configuration
- Authentication flow (OAuth or API token)
- API request/response handling
- Rate limiting and retry logic
- Error handling for API failures
- Data mapping between Notion structures and CLI representations
- Pagination handling for large datasets
- Webhook handling if real-time updates are required

The implementation must adhere to Notion API best practices, handle edge cases gracefully, and provide a clean abstraction layer that the rest of the CLI can use without worrying about API details.

Security is paramount: API credentials must be stored securely, and the integration should follow principle of least privilege when requesting Notion permissions.
tasks.task_notes: The Notion API integration is a high-risk area that requires expertise. The Technical Lead should personally implement this given its criticality. Consider using official Notion SDK if available for the chosen language, or implement a robust custom client if not. Test thoroughly with different Notion workspace configurations. Handle API versioning and backwards compatibility. The integration should be thoroughly documented as it will be used throughout the codebase.

tasks.description:
As specified in the Technical Lead responsibilities (section 6.2.2), define performance standards for the CLI tool and establish oversight processes to ensure they are met.

Performance standards should cover:
- Command execution time targets (e.g., basic commands < 100ms, API operations < 2s)
- Memory usage limits
- Startup time benchmarks
- API request efficiency (minimize unnecessary calls)
- Caching strategies to improve perceived performance
- Progress indicators for long-running operations
- Performance testing methodology
- Performance regression detection in CI/CD

For a CLI tool, perceived performance is critical to user satisfaction. Users expect command-line tools to be fast and responsive. The standards should be realistic given the need to interact with external APIs (Notion) but should push the team to optimize where possible.

The Technical Lead should establish performance benchmarks early, implement monitoring, and review performance in code reviews.
tasks.task_notes: Performance standards should be documented and measurable. Consider using performance budgets and automated performance testing in CI. For API integrations, implement smart caching to reduce latency. Profile the application to identify bottlenecks. The balance between performance and feature richness should be guided by user needs as identified by the Product Manager.

tasks.description:
As specified in the Technical Lead responsibilities (section 6.2.2), define security standards for the CLI tool and establish oversight processes to ensure they are met.

Security standards should address:
- Secure storage of API credentials and sensitive data
- Input validation and sanitization
- Protection against injection attacks
- Secure communication with Notion API (HTTPS, certificate validation)
- Principle of least privilege for Notion permissions
- Secure handling of user data and privacy
- Dependency security (monitoring for vulnerabilities)
- Security testing and vulnerability scanning
- Incident response procedures
- Security code review guidelines

For a CLI tool that integrates with user Notion workspaces, security is paramount. Users are trusting the tool with access to potentially sensitive information. The security standards should meet or exceed industry best practices.

The Technical Lead should conduct security reviews of all code, especially authentication, API integration, and data handling logic.
tasks.task_notes: Security should be built in from the start, not bolted on later. Consider common CLI security issues: credential leakage in logs, insecure file permissions, command injection vulnerabilities. Use established security libraries rather than rolling custom crypto. Plan for security audits before launch. The Technical Lead should stay informed about Notion API security requirements and updates.

tasks.task_name: Establish developer mentoring and knowledge sharing framework
tasks.description:
As specified in the Technical Lead responsibilities (section 6.2.2), establish a mentoring framework and knowledge sharing practices for the development team.

The framework should include:
- Onboarding process for new team members
- Pair programming practices and scheduling
- Knowledge sharing sessions (e.g., tech talks, architecture reviews)
- Documentation standards for sharing technical knowledge
- Code review as mentoring opportunity
- Technical skills development plan
- Problem-solving and debugging guidance
- Best practices library and reference materials

With 2-3 developers (2 Backend/CLI Developers + Technical Lead contributing code) on a small team, effective mentoring ensures consistent quality, knowledge distribution, and team growth. The Technical Lead should create an environment where developers feel comfortable asking questions and learning from each other.

The framework should be lightweight and integrated into daily work rather than creating separate overhead.
tasks.task_notes: Mentoring is an investment that pays off in team capability and code quality. The Technical Lead should allocate time for mentoring activities without letting it interfere with critical development work. Consider rotating pair programming partners to spread knowledge. Use code reviews as teaching moments. Create internal documentation that captures architectural decisions and patterns. Track team members' growth and adjust mentoring approach as needed.
